title: Kitchaminchok
summary: A Moriches Island boundary placename appearing in seventeenth-century whaling and estate records, with related forms including Ketchininchoge and Cochiminchoake.
address_label: Moriches Island, Moriches Bay, East Moriches, NY (approximate)
map_geometry_source: Approximate/general point for Moriches Island at East Moriches in Great South Bay; not a surveyed island boundary.
why_this_matters: Recognized as a sacred Unkechaug drift whaling site, Kitchaminchok served as a key boundary marker where early colonial agreements set a strict price of five English pounds for every harvested whale. Documenting these early commercial transactions reveals how Native peoples attempted to negotiate the aggressive expansion of the European market while trying to maintain access to their traditional coastal resources.
introduction_content: Kitchaminchok is the primary recorded placename for Moriches Island at East Moriches. The island is described as lying on the north shore of the Great South Bay, separated from the mainland by a narrow strait, with meadowland and a small pond.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Kitchaminchok, Ketchininchoge, Kitchaminchoke, Kitchaminfchoke, Kitche-minchoake, Cochiminchoake, and Chikemenckoake. The name is interpreted as a boundary designation meaning the beginning island, from a first element connected with beginning and a second element for island.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are powerful, and their significance extends far beyond words. Learning and embracing the original Indigenous phrases used to describe the world around us acknowledges the impact of colonization, recognizes First Peoples’ ongoing relationship to the land, and honours their traditional way of being.”

— C’tasi:a (Geraldine Manson), Snuneymuxw Mulstimuxw: Sacred Place Names, their Travels, and Stories (2023), New Society Publishers book description, opening paragraph
land_loss_content: Kitchaminchok links Moriches Island to Indigenous whaling rights, sachemship, colonial grants, lawsuits, and wills. Keeping its related forms together helps show how one island could appear under several spellings across different records.
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is a general point for Moriches Island at East Moriches in the Great South Bay. It orients the placename without trace the island boundary or the full whaling-rights corridor.
